title: Comparison of native and canonical global projection mates without slice data
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $R,S$ sheaves of commutative rings on their native small pro-etale sites, and $c:f^{-1}R\cong S$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $a,b$ be native derived tensor models normalized on flat-term K-flat representatives [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $g$ be any normalized global ProjectionRestriction.Global package for these same data [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-restriction]. Write $L,D$ for native derived pullback and direct image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and $L_g,D_g,T^Y_g,T^X_g$ for those of g. For any $E\in D(S)$ there are natural isomorphisms $s:a(DE,-)\cong T^Y_g(D_gE,-)$ and $t:D(b(E,L(-)))\cong D_g(T^X_g(E,L_g(-)))$ such that $\pi^{native}_{E,P};t_P=s_P;\pi^g_{E,P}$ for every $P\in D(R)$. Both projection arrows are the actual adjoint-of-counit maps [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. This asserts no slice presentation and no shift or exactness structures.

proof.text: The descent bijection of each supplied canonical tensor model makes restriction to resolving pairs fully faithful. Lift the composite of the inverse native representative isomorphism and the supplied representative isomorphism to natural tensor isomorphisms ea and eb, retaining their representative equations.

The coefficient equality determines the Operation record, whose remaining fields are propositions. Identify it with the already constructed globalOperation. Two OrdinaryTensor records for this operation are equal: transpose their components under the module adjunction and use pure-tensor extensionality and their identical pure_unit equations. Thus the given ordinary comparison equals the existing globalOrdinaryTensor, explicitly transported from the native ordinary comparison through left-adjoint uniqueness.

Write e for ordinary left-adjoint uniqueness. The explicit construction of globalOrdinaryTensor transports the native comparison through e. Tensor naturality and cancellation give e(M tensor N);mu_native = mu_global;tensor(e(M),e(N)).

Apply the proved proEtaleTensorComparisonTransport theorem with the ordinary isomorphism e and its exact-derived isomorphism. The exact-derived factorization equation supplies its normalization hypothesis. The previously lifted tensor isomorphisms ea,eb supply its representative equations. This yields the derived tensor square needed for the mate calculation.

Conjugate the derived pullback isomorphism under the two actual derived adjunctions to obtain a right-adjoint isomorphism. Curry ea and compose it with this right-adjoint isomorphism to construct s. Construct t by first changing the right adjoint, then eb, then the inverse pullback isomorphism. Apply the proved abstract projection-mate square theorem with the two horizontal functors equal to identities and with the tensor square just proved. Its conjugate is exactly the selected right-adjoint isomorphism; simplifying its identity unitors gives the required component equation.

lean.statement:
theorem proEtaleProjectionGlobalComparison
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (S : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1})
    (c : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage f CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj R ≅ S)
    (a : ProEtaleTensorModel Y R) (b : ProEtaleTensorModel X S)
    (g : Global f R S c) (E : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X S)) :
    ∃ s : (Functor.curryObj a.tensor).obj
        ((proEtaleRingDerivedDirectImage f R S c).obj E) ≅
      (Functor.curryObj g.tensorY.functor).obj (g.operation.right.obj E),
    ∃ t : (proEtaleRingDerivedPullback f R S c ⋙
        (Functor.curryObj b.tensor).obj E ⋙ proEtaleRingDerivedDirectImage f R S c) ≅
      (g.operation.left ⋙ (Functor.curryObj g.tensorX.functor).obj E ⋙ g.operation.right),
    ∀ P : Der R,
      proEtaleProjectionFormulaMate f R S c a b E P ≫ t.hom.app P =
        s.hom.app P ≫ derivedProjectionFormulaMate g.operation.left g.operation.right
          g.operation.derivedAdjunction g.tensorY.functor g.tensorX.functor
          g.tensorComparison.comparison E P
